canonical_name: Schoen theorem (Yamabe problem, conformally flat case)
canonical_statement: Provisional source-level scope: if M is a smooth compact manifold without boundary, of dimension n at least 3, and g is a locally conformally flat Riemannian metric on M, then the conformal class of g contains a smooth Riemannian metric of constant scalar curvature.
domain_and_universes: A finite-dimensional smooth compact boundaryless manifold M, dimension n >= 3, with a smooth locally conformally flat Riemannian metric g; exact Lean universe and typeclass presentation remain open.
quantifiers: M: smooth compact n-manifold without boundary
g: smooth locally conformally flat Riemannian metric on M
conclusion: There exists a smooth positive conformal factor u such that the metric conformal to g by u has constant scalar curvature; the exponent convention and connectedness convention must be fixed in the statement phase.

alternate_encodings.target: existence of a positive smooth solution of the Yamabe equation
alternate_encodings.relationship: classically equivalent after the conformal scalar-curvature transformation law

alternate_encodings.target: attainment of the Yamabe functional in the conformal class
alternate_encodings.relationship: variational formulation leading to a constant-scalar-curvature conformal metric

excluded_degenerate_cases: Dimensions zero, one, and two are outside this Yamabe formulation. Noncompact manifolds and manifolds with boundary are excluded. No uniqueness, sign prescription, normalized volume, or full unrestricted Yamabe theorem is claimed.
foundation_profile: Not instantiated; classical analysis, choice, quotient/manifold, elliptic PDE, and geometric-analysis dependencies require audit.
